source.title: The Inductive Bias of Convolutional Neural Networks: Locality and Weight Sharing Reshape Implicit Regularization
source.authors: Tong-Tong Liang; Esha Singh; Rahul Parhi; Alexander Cloninger; Yu-Xiang Wang

page_placements.theme: Noisy interpolation generalizes only under stated conditions

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, though some equations and figure text are garbled by extraction. No missing section prevents assessing the claim versions relevant here.
record.tranche_reason: The paper's own experiments and theory refine the broad memorization/generalization claim: a sparse network can interpolate arbitrary labels in a specified patch geometry, while another sparse network resists overfitting noisy labels. It does not test all six versions in their stated original settings.
record.gate_note: Relevant results are theoretical interpolation under a patch-isolation condition (Theorem 4.3 and Figure 3), and CIFAR-10 noisy-label regression comparing SCN and FCN (Figure 5). Neither experiment tests completely random labeling of the training images as a classification task with the original architecture and optimizer settings. Figure 7 reports FCN memorization on spherical regression data, not the V1 random-label claim. The cited claims about fitting pure noise and Arpit et al. are prior work, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study measures interpolation and generalization in two-layer regression networks trained on signal plus Gaussian target noise. It does not test completely random labeling, any specified input corruption with fitting measurements, a label-corruption fraction sweep, explicit regularization comparisons, or signal-versus-noise learning order. Its arbitrary-label interpolation theorem establishes existence of stable parameters, not that stochastic gradient training reaches them under an unchanged recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that patch geometry governs the strength of the stability-induced constraint: concentrated projected patches yield generalization bounds, whereas isolatable patches permit constructed stable interpolants of arbitrary bounded targets. Their CIFAR-10 regression experiment shows the SCN resisting noise interpolation while the FCN interpolates.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies two-layer ReLU networks under full-batch gradient descent and a below-edge-of-stability analysis. Its experiments use synthetic spherical regression and CIFAR-10 regression with noisy targets, rather than the original random-label classification protocol or its stated optimizer settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Patch geometry changes the outcome: structured spherical projections and CIFAR-10 convolutional patches support generalization, while random spherical patches permit interpolation; SCN and FCN differ on CIFAR-10 noisy regression.

fits_no_version.finding: The SCN interpolates noisy regression targets with independently sampled spherical patches while sharpness remains near 2/η.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse two-layer networks can memorize additive regression noise near the edge of stability when patch geometry permits isolation.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10 teacher-generated regression targets with Gaussian noise, the SCN remains near the noise floor and achieves lower excess risk while the FCN interpolates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse connectivity can reduce regression-noise memorization and excess risk under the tested patch geometry and training conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: The spherical-input FCN reaches training loss 0.0006 with excess risk 0.8745 despite stability near the threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stability alone does not prevent memorization of additive regression noise by two-layer fully connected networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 4.3 constructs a width-at-most-n interpolant with bounded sharpness when each nonzero-labeled example has a unique unit-norm patch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Patch isolation permits stable interpolation of arbitrary bounded targets; this existence result does not establish optimization accessibility.

record.problems: The experimental networks are two-layer regression models, and results do not test the original random-label image classification protocol. Noisy targets are generated by a frozen SCN plus Gaussian noise, and no corruption-fraction sweep is reported. Several result values appear only in figures; the paper supplies qualitative descriptions, not numeric values for all comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-bearing result rows identified beyond the extracted interpolation, CIFAR-10 noisy-regression comparison, and spherical-regression memorization results. Figure 2 and Table 3 concern generalization-gap scaling on synthetic spherical data, not any named version's random-label or fitting behavior.

untested.parts: Training standard deep networks on completely random labels with an unchanged architecture and training recipe, reaching near-zero training error and chance test performance.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence slowdown as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs. Appendix G.3's shuffled-pixel control measures geometry only.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across a sweep from zero to complete random-label corruption.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy labels. The regression training curves do not separately measure signal and noise acquisition.

record.verdict_notes: The extraction's V1 support and V4 scope limitation should be removed. These are adjacent regression and stability findings, not tests of the specified versions; their untested components do not justify limits_scope.

versions.untested_parts: The paper shows interpolation of arbitrary labels by an SCN under an explicit single-patch-isolation condition, but does not test completely random labeling of the original training images under the original network and optimizer settings, nor report test error at chance.
No comparison of time to fit true versus random labels or convergence slowdown by corrupted-label fraction.
No test of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs for fitting error.

The CIFAR-10 experiment uses noisy regression targets generated from a frozen SCN plus Gaussian noise; it does not sweep the fraction of randomly corrupted labels from none to all or measure the claimed steady test-error trajectory.
No comparison isolating weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation as factors in fitting random labels and generalizing on true labels.
No measurement of learning order or comparison of when real versus random labels are learned.

conditions.value: independently sampled from the unit sphere and concatenated

rows.measure: Training loss and interpolation of labels
rows.locator: Figure 3; experimental details in Appendix G.2
rows.note: The authors describe rapid interpolation of labels; these are noisy regression labels in an explicitly constructed random spherical-patch setting, not a test of completely random image labels under the claim's original settings.
rows.check: Figure 3 demonstrates interpolation of signal-plus-noise regression targets, not completely random labels. The reported Train MSE of 1.0418 measures error against the clean ground-truth function under Eq. 131; it is not residual error against the noisy training targets.

rows.locator: Figure 5; experimental details in Appendix G.4
rows.note: The result is noisy regression with Gaussian target noise, not a sweep of randomly corrupted label fractions or a report that training error remains perfect.
rows.check: The SCN's training loss remains near the noise floor in a fixed Gaussian-noise regression task. This does not measure V4's randomly corrupted label fractions or classification test-error trajectory.

relation.reason: The study discusses noise memorization and its relation to architectural implicit regularization, without directly testing V1–V6 or using random-label fitting as a tool.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure signal-plus-Gaussian-noise regression; the interpolation theorem constructs stable solutions without showing gradient descent learns completely random labels. Neither tests a listed claim version.
